title: Raw vs Pasteurized Milk: What Changes and Why It Matters

seo.title: Raw vs Pasteurized Milk: Safety and Nutrition
seo.meta_description: Pasteurization sharply reduces pathogens with only small nutritional changes. Raw milk can carry Salmonella, Campylobacter, E. coli, or Listeria while looking normal.
seo.search_intent: Compare raw and pasteurized milk by food safety, nutrition, and practical differences.

excerpt: Pasteurization uses controlled heat to destroy disease-causing microorganisms while leaving protein, minerals, fat, and calories largely unchanged. Raw milk can carry dangerous bacteria without any unusual smell or appearance, so its microbiological risk is substantially higher.
content_html:
Raw milk can look, smell, and taste completely normal while carrying pathogens. The most important raw-versus-pasteurized difference is microbiological safety, not a major nutrient loss.

What pasteurization does

Controlled time-and-temperature combinations kill organisms such as Salmonella, Campylobacter, Shiga toxin-producing E. coli, and Listeria. Pasteurization does not sterilize milk, which is why refrigerated milk remains perishable.

Major nutrients barely change

Protein, fat, lactose, calcium, and other minerals remain essentially intact. There can be small reductions in selected heat-sensitive vitamins, but those differences do not offset the foodborne-illness risk of untreated milk.

Risk is especially important for vulnerable people

Children, pregnant people, older adults, and anyone with a weakened immune system have greater risk of severe outcomes from foodborne infection. U.S. rules on raw-milk sales vary by state, but federal authorities consistently warn against drinking it.

For everyday consumption, pasteurized milk provides the nutritional role of milk with far lower microbiological risk.

faq.question: Does raw milk have more nutrients?
faq.answer: Some heat-sensitive vitamins can differ slightly, but protein, minerals, fat, and calories are very similar.

faq.question: Can you smell dangerous bacteria in raw milk?
faq.answer: No. Pathogens can be present without visible or sensory signs.

faq.question: Does pasteurization sterilize milk?
faq.answer: No. It greatly reduces pathogens, but pasteurized milk still needs refrigeration and has a finite shelf life.
